name: Mauritius

findings.local_actor: Mauritius Police Force / Mauritius Telecom (prime contractor)
findings.builder: Mauritius Telecom (prime contractor; five subcontractors incl. Huawei)
findings.summary: The Safe City programme, about 4,000 intelligent CCTV cameras plus police radio trunking, was implemented by state-linked Mauritius Telecom with Huawei among subcontractors under a 20-year operating lease of roughly Rs 21bn, operational since August 2019.

sources.publisher: AllAfrica (French; original Mauritian outlet not named)

findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc on the equipment rule: Huawei is described as key partner for the all-cloud video platform (StratNews/Le Matinal) and as a named subcontractor (AllAfrica); exact Huawei scope vs other subcontractors not established, and Huawei's own case studies were not fetched (banned). No opened S1/S2 source, so not corroborated; low. Rs 21bn not converted (no source-date rate); AfricLaw lease schedule (USD 13m then 18.9m/23.9m a year) not used as a value. AllAfrica story id suggests March 2025, when the PM said he envisaged an independent evaluation; no cancellation found, but continued operation as of the run date not confirmed, so still_current null. Pre-2020 date: map will halve unless confirmed current.

findings.summary: Huawei Marine built the 700-730 km, 16 Tbps Mauritius and Rodrigues Submarine cable (MARS) with PCCW Global for Mauritius Telecom, using Huawei 100G WDM transmission; the project was reported completed ahead of schedule in 2019.

sources.publisher: SubTel Forum (republished Huawei Marine/PCCW press release)

findings.analyst_inference: Cable equipment vendor Huawei Marine, so pole prc; owner Mauritius Telecom inferred from DCD quote. SubTel item is a vendor press release, so S4 and not counted; uncorroborated, low. Tier 5 = completion reported in the release; RFS date and current status not independently confirmed. Domestic link to Rodrigues, not an international route.

findings.summary: NEC XON, Emtel's integration partner since 2011, upgraded cell sites for 5G and the backbone to 100G, with Juniper equipment forming the network core; radio vendor not named.
findings.analyst_inference: Appears to be NEC XON marketing material republished; Total Telecom coded S2 but may be a press release, reviewer may downgrade. Juniper (US) core sets pole us; NEC XON (South African arm of Japan's NEC) is integrator. Date approximate: article cites Q2-Q3 2023 Ookla award and 2024 plans, no publication date shown. Tier 3 assumed for an operating vendor relationship; no award notice seen. Single opened source; low.

findings.controller: Mauritius Telecom (mytGPT); underlying model provider not stated
findings.summary: Mauritius's Education Ministry launched mytGPT for Education, built with Mauritius Telecom for students, teachers and parents, after an August-October 2025 pilot with about 70 Grade 12 students.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the opened source does not say which model underlies mytGPT or who holds the weights; it may be a domestic wrapper over a foreign API. Tier 2: pilot completed and launch announced; national usage not shown. Mauritius Telecom is state-linked with Orange holding a 40% stake (DCD tag page, June 2024), which complicates any domestic coding.

facilities.null_reason: one search plus DCD Mauritius tag page: only opinion pieces on a digital-hub ambition and cable/operator items since 2023; no data-centre or AI-campus project with a named controller

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase surfaced in facilities or models searches
